English සිංහල தமிழ் Fact Checked All Economy Society Environment Politics Health Methodology About Us Explore Fact-Checking Contact Us #fakenews The Arunata Pera program is not only for Malima families False It is being exchanged in social media that the children's hair cutting programs are being implemented in the families associated with the Compass. by Anonymous | February 7, 2024 Fact Seeker also observed how various people have given critical comments regarding this post and looked into this matter. It appears that the “Compass Related Families” section of this post has been edited. Has a post like this been published by the National People’s Force? Fact Seeker made an inquiry in this regard to the media section of the National People’s Power. There, they stated that the National People’s Power is implementing a social care program called “Arunata Pera” where free haircuts will be done for school children. The media department stated that a poster has also been created in this regard. But they also stated that it is not only for the children of Malima and that the actual poster has been edited and this poster has been published with those changes. Accordingly, Fact Seeker confirms that this is a fake post. Latest updates #misleading Did Sri Lankan MPs Receive a Rs. 60,000 Salary Increase? We are an independent fact-checking team affiliated with the Sri Lanka Press Institute(SLPI). The objective and long-term goal of the FactSeeker is to provide the public with reliable and verified content in the attempt of debunking mis/disinformation. The unit, with the SLPI, is committed to contributing to improved media literacy in Sri Lanka.
